D009-D011_h001.question:
It’s kind of like I’ve been living in two different gears the past year.

Most of the time this last year, I’ve been really low. I used to be proud of my clearance rate, my instincts, but now even when I close a case, I feel… nothing. My wife will congratulate me and I just shrug. Getting through a simple report feels like wading through mud—my brain tires out so fast I have to reread the same sentence over and over. A couple months back it got so dark I started hoarding my old pain meds, thinking if it got bad enough, I’d just take them all. That scared my wife when she found them. I’ve been calling in sick more, missing deadlines. It’s affecting the job.

But about a month ago, before this low patch got worse, I had this stretch where I was on edge and wired. I’d snap at colleagues over nothing, talk nonstop in briefing, pacing the room, bouncing my leg, unable to sit still. I barely slept and didn’t feel like I needed it. My mind was racing with ideas—none of it really tied to worry, just this urge to move, to do, to talk. I do get anxious—especially about my cases and my family’s safety—but those “amped up” times feel separate from the usual worrying, like my brain’s flooring it on its own.
D009-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009-D011_h002.question:
It’s kind of hard to explain, because I feel like two different people.

For most of this past year I’ve just been… down. It’s like this heavy, gray feeling that doesn’t lift. Stuff that should matter, like finishing a big job on site or getting praised by the foreman, barely registers. I just think, “Whatever, who cares.” I’m tired all the time, even on days I actually sleep 8–9 hours. Just walking up the scaffolding feels like I’ve already done a full shift. A few months ago I’d actually started putting aside pain pills from jobs and had this plan to take them all one night. I didn’t go through with it, but it got that far.

But then about a month ago, I flipped the other way. I got really edgy and snappy over tiny things—if a guy on site moved slow, I’d blow up. I couldn’t sit still; on breaks I’d be pacing, finding extra tasks, asking for more shifts, trying to start side projects after work. I’d sleep maybe 2–3 hours, sometimes none, and feel like I didn’t need it. My head would race with ideas and I’d talk nonstop, like I couldn’t shut up or tolerate silence. I do feel a bit anxious here and there, but the racing thoughts and that push to keep doing stuff come on their own, even when I’m not particularly worried about anything.
D009-D011_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009-D011_h003.question:

D009-D011_h006.question:
I’ve been having these stretches where I feel like two different people.  

A few months ago, for about two months, I was…almost too “up.” I’d be chipper one minute and snapping at my daughter on the phone the next, for no real reason. Then I “crash.” For the last two months I’ve mostly felt flat, like everything is behind glass. I wake up at 4 a.m. every day and can’t get back to sleep. I’m anxious and tense a lot, but it’s more this heavy emptiness. I’ve stopped going to church, missing my senior group—just don’t have it in me.
